items.title: Sexual Misconduct's Remaining Seven Elements: Coercion, Secrecy, and Wrong Time, Place, or Manner

items.zh: 他妻妾者，謂已適他。他所攝者，謂即未適他，為三守護之所守護。若由凶詐者，謂矯亂已而行邪行。若由強力者，謂對父母等公然強逼。若由隱伏者，謂不對彼，竊相欣欲。
items.en: "Another's wife or concubine" means one already given in marriage. "Belonging to another" means one not yet married, but under the three kinds of protection just described. "Through deception" means beguiling and confusing her before committing the act. "Through force" means openly coercing her parents and the like. "Through concealment" means, without informing them, secretly indulging mutual desire.

items.zh: 而行欲行者，謂兩兩交會。即於此事非理欲心而行邪行者，謂於非道、非處非時，自妻妾所而為罪失。
items.en: "Committing the sexual act" means the actual union of two persons. "Acting on an improper desire even within this same matter" means committing an offence even with one's own wife or concubine, if done through an improper bodily manner, in an improper place, or at an improper time.

items.zh: 此中略義者，謂略顯示若彼所行、若行差別、若欲邪行應知。
items.en: The brief meaning here is this: it shows, in summary, the object towards which the act is directed, the manner in which it is carried out, and what actually constitutes the offence of sexual misconduct itself.

items.title: False Speech Opens: The Many Settings Where a Lie Can Be Told

items.zh: 復次，諸妄語者者，此是總句。若王者，謂王家。若彼使者，謂執理家。若別者，謂長者居士。若眾者，謂彼聚集。
items.en: Further, "those who speak falsely" is the summary phrase. "Before the king" means in a royal court. "Before his officials" means before those who administer the law. "Before an individual" means before an elder or householder. "Before an assembly" means before a gathered crowd.

items.title: False Speech Completed: Fear, Greed, and the Deliberate Concealment of One's Own Mind

items.zh: 若大集中者，謂四方人眾聚集處。若已知者，謂隨前三所經語言。若已見者，謂隨曾見所經語言。若由自因者，謂或因怖畏，或因味著。如由自因，他因亦爾。因怖畏者，謂由怖畏殺、縛、治罰、黜責等故。因味著者，謂為財穀、珍寶等故。
items.en: "Before a great assembly" means a gathering of people from every direction. "Regarding what is already known" means speaking contrary to what was learned through hearing, sensing, or cognizing in any of the settings above. "Regarding what is already seen" means speaking contrary to what was directly witnessed. "Through one's own cause" means either out of fear or out of attachment to gain — and the same holds when the cause comes from another. "Out of fear" means dreading being killed, bound, punished, or dismissed and disgraced. "Out of attachment" means craving wealth, grain, or treasure.

items.zh: 知而說妄語者，謂覆想欲見而說語言。此中略義者，謂依處故、異說故、因緣故、壞想故，而說妄語應知。
items.en: "Knowingly speaking falsely" means concealing one's actual perception, intention, or view, and speaking otherwise. The brief meaning here, then, is that false speech should be understood through its setting, its contrariness to what was actually known, its underlying cause, and its deliberate corruption of one's own perception.

items.title: Divisive Speech: The Deliberate Art of Breaking Others Apart

items.zh: 復次，離間語者者，此是總句。若為破壞者，謂由破壞意樂故。聞彼語已向此宣說，聞此語已向彼宣說者，謂隨所聞順乖離語。破壞和合者，謂能生起喜別離故。
items.en: Further, "one who speaks divisively" is the summary phrase. "Intending to break apart" means acting with the deliberate wish to cause a rift. "Hearing this and reporting it there, hearing that and reporting it here" means selectively passing along, in either direction, whatever was heard that tends towards estrangement. "Breaking apart harmony" means bringing about a positive delight in separation between two parties.

items.zh: 隨印別離者，謂能乖違喜更生故。憙壞和合者，謂於已生喜別離中心染污故。樂印別離者，謂於乖違喜更生中心染污故。說能離間語者，謂或不聞，或他方便故。
items.en: "Reinforcing an existing rift" means causing a delight in continued estrangement to arise anew. "Delighting in breaking apart harmony" means taking a defiled pleasure in a delight in separation one has already caused to arise. "Delighting in reinforcing a rift" means taking a defiled pleasure in a renewed delight in continued estrangement. "Speaking what functions as divisive speech" means either "not hearing," or dividing them through some other means.

items.title: Harsh Speech, Told in Reverse: Twelve Marks of a Bodhisattva's Genuine Speech

items.zh: 此中略義者，謂略顯示離間意樂、離間未壞方便、離間已壞方便、離間染污心，及他方便應知。復次，麁惡語者者，此是總句。此中尸羅支所攝故，名語無擾動。文句美滑，故名悅耳。增上欲解所發起故，非假偽故，非諂媚故，名為稱心。
items.en: The brief meaning here shows: the intention to divide, the means used before any rift exists, the means used to deepen a rift already present, the defiled delight taken in either, and indirect means — these should be understood together. Further, "one who speaks harshly" is the summary phrase. Because it belongs to genuine moral discipline, such speech is called undisturbing. Because its words are gracious and smooth, it is called pleasant to hear. Because it arises from a firm, wholehearted conviction, is never false, and never flatters, it is called heart-satisfying.

items.zh: 不增益故，應順時機，引義利故，名為可愛。趣涅槃宮，故名先首。文句可味，故名美妙。
items.en: Because it neither exaggerates nor overstates, and because it is timely and brings genuine benefit, it is called lovable. Because it leads towards the palace of nirvāṇa, it is called foremost. Because its words are genuinely satisfying to take in, it is called beautiful.

items.title: The Remaining Six Marks, and Speech Regrouped Into Three Kinds

items.zh: 善釋文句，故名分明。顯然有趣，故名易可解了。攝受正法，故名可施功勞。離愛味心之所發起，故名無所依止。不過度量，故名非可厭逆。相續廣大，故名無邊無盡。
items.en: Because it explains its own words and phrases well, it is called clear. Because it is plainly evident and genuinely engaging, it is called easy to understand. Because it draws the listener into taking up the true Dharma, it is called worth the effort. Because it arises free of any craving for personal gain, it is called without attachment. Because it never exceeds its proper measure, it is called never tiresome. Because it flows on, sustained and expansive, it is called boundless and inexhaustible.

items.zh: 又從無擾動語乃至無邊無盡語，應知略攝為三種語。一、尸羅律儀所攝語，謂一種。
items.en: Further, from "undisturbing speech" through "boundless and inexhaustible speech," it should be understood that these are, in brief, subsumed under three kinds of speech. The first kind, speech subsumed under moral discipline, comprises the first alone.

items.title: Three Kinds Become Three Again: Language That Ripens Towards Nirvāṇa Itself

items.zh: 二、等歡喜語，謂三種。三、說法語，謂其所餘。即此最後又有三種應知。一、所趣圓滿語謂初一。二、文詞圓滿語，謂次二。三、方便圓滿語，謂其所餘。
items.en: The second kind, speech that brings equal delight, comprises three of the marks. The third kind, speech that teaches the Dharma, comprises the remaining eight. This last kind should further be understood to divide into three: first, speech perfect in its ultimate destination, comprising the first of the eight; second, speech perfect in its wording, comprising the next two; third, speech perfect in its skilful means, comprising the rest.

items.zh: 又於未來世可愛樂故，名可愛語。於過去世可愛樂故，名可樂語。於現在世事及領受可愛樂故，名可欣語及可意語。應知即等歡喜語，名無量眾生可愛、可樂、可欣、可意語。即說法語，名三摩呬多語。即尸羅支所攝語，名由無悔等漸次能引三摩地語。
items.en: Further: cherished by beings of the future, it is called lovable speech. Cherished by beings of the past, it is called delightful speech. Cherished by beings in the present, both as spoken and as received, it is called joyous and gratifying speech. It should be understood that this is precisely the same as speech bringing equal delight — cherished, delightful, joyous, and gratifying to countless beings across all three times. Speech that teaches the Dharma is precisely what is called samādhi-inducing speech. And speech subsumed under moral discipline is precisely what, through freedom from regret and what naturally follows from it, gradually leads to concentration itself.

items.title: Harsh Speech Named Directly at Last: The Sting and the Blow

items.zh: 此中毒螫語者，謂毀摩他言，縱瞋毒故。麁獷語者，謂惱亂他言，發苦觸故。所餘麁惡語，翻前白品應知。
items.en: Here, "venomous speech" means words that insult and demean another, indulging the poison of one's own hatred. "Coarse, brutal speech" means words that disturb and provoke another, inflicting a genuinely painful impact. As for the remaining kinds of harsh speech, they should be understood simply as the reverse of every one of the twelve wholesome marks already described.

items.title: Frivolous Speech Opens: Five Ways an Accusation Can Itself Go Wrong

items.zh: 復次，諸綺語者者，此是總句。於邪舉罪時，有五種邪舉罪者。言不應時故，名非時語者。言不實故，名非實語者。
items.en: Further, "those who speak frivolously" is the summary phrase. When bringing an improper accusation, there are five kinds of improper accuser. Because the words are spoken at the wrong time, this is called speaking untimely. Because the words are untrue, this is called speaking falsely.

blocks.text: Today covers the third course of action and most of the four kinds of wrong speech. The most beautiful passage is the account of harsh speech, which the treatise describes in reverse: as twelve marks of a bodhisattva's genuine speech. Master Cháng Bǎi: it does so "because this treatise belongs to the Mahāyāna bodhisattva canon."

An unmarried woman is under three kinds of protection: by her relatives (or herself), by the law, and by gatekeepers. Misconduct includes approaching someone so protected, or another's spouse, by deception, force, or concealment. Master Cháng Bǎi's examples: deception such as drugging; force such as the powerful pressuring a family into a marriage; concealment such as a secret affair hidden from the family.

Even with one's own spouse, the wrong manner, place, or time is misconduct. Master Cháng Bǎi lists improper times: during menstruation, late in pregnancy, while nursing, while keeping the fast-day precepts, or during illness. The principle is respect for the other's condition.

False speech is described by its setting (a royal court, before officials, before an elder, before an assembly) and by the four bases of speech from Day 15: seen, heard, sensed, known. Venerable Miào Jìng maps them: seeing is the eye; hearing, the ear; sensing, nose, tongue, and body; knowing, the mind.

It is summarised by four points: setting, contrary speech, cause (fear, greed), and the deliberate concealment of one's own perception, intention, or view. Venerable Miào Jìng's story: Maudgalyāyana predicted rain that did not come. Asked with what mind he spoke, he said he had said what he truly thought, and the Buddha ruled it was not false speech. A mistake is not a lie; a lie conceals one's own mind.

Divisive speech is "the deliberate art of breaking others apart": hearing two people praise each other and pretending not to have heard, so as not to reconcile them (the *Pīxún jì*'s reading); or speaking to split those who are united.

Instead of portraying the harsh speaker, the treatise lists twelve marks of genuine speech, among them speech that is pleasing to hear, gentle, clear, timely, honest, beneficial, and, last, speech "leading to the palace of nirvāṇa", called "foremost". Venerable Miào Jìng: the earlier marks belong to the path of favourable rebirth; the last to the path of liberation.

The twelve are grouped into three: speech of moral discipline (one), speech that brings equal delight (three), and speech teaching the Dharma (eight). The last is called *samāhita*, "evenly drawn" speech. Master Cháng Bǎi: disciplined speech "gradually leads to concentration through freedom from regret", which is why discipline heads the three trainings.

Only then does the treatise name harsh speech directly: "venomous" and "coarse". Master Cháng Bǎi: venomous speech is "like a bee sting, very painful, swelling at once"; coarse speech is "like being cut by a knife".

Frivolous speech opens with five ways an accusation can go wrong: at the wrong time, untrue, unhelpful, harsh, or angry. Master Cháng Bǎi gives the positive form from the vinaya: one who admonishes another should speak at the right time, truthfully, for the other's benefit, gently, and with compassion. It is a good checklist for any correction we give.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what three kinds of protection does an unmarried woman have?
options: by revered relatives (or herself), by the king or magistrates, by gatekeepers
quiz.why: "This briefly shows three kinds of protection for an unmarried woman: first, protection by revered close relatives or by herself; second, protection by the king or ruling authority; third, protection by those who guard the gate." Master Cháng Bǎi: kings, ministers, judges, and police protect by law; gatekeepers make intrusion hard.

quiz.q: The text says even with one's own spouse, improper manner, place, or time is an offence. What "improper times" does Master Cháng Bǎi list?
options: during menstruation, late pregnancy, nursing, while observing fast-day precepts, or when ill
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "When she is menstruating, when the pregnancy is at full term, while nursing, while observing fast-day precepts, or when ill." And: "Even with one's own wife, doing so carries fault." Venerable Miào Jìng agrees: lawful spouses can still err.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, in what settings may false speech occur?
options: the royal court, officials, an individual elder or householder, an assembly, a great gathering from all directions
quiz.why: "'Before the king' means in a royal court. 'Before his officials' means before those who administer the law. 'Before an individual' means before an elder or householder. 'Before an assembly' means before a gathered crowd." §33: "a great assembly" is people from every direction. Master Cháng Bǎi: anyone enforcing the king's law is an official.

quiz.q: The text says knowing false speech means concealing one's perception, intention, or view. Venerable Miào Jìng tells of Maudgalyāyana predicting rain in seven days that didn't come. How did the Buddha judge it?
options: Maudgalyāyana said what he truly thought, so the Buddha ruled it was not false speech
the Buddha called it a grave lie
the Buddha said it rained later
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "'With what mind did you say it?' 'With a true mind — I said what I thought.' The Buddha said this was not false speech." The key is concealing one's actual perception, intention, or view; being wrong isn't lying.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, through what four points is false speech summarised?
options: setting, contrary speech, cause, corrupting one's own perception
quiz.why: "False speech should be understood through its setting, its contrariness to what was actually known, its underlying cause, and its deliberate corruption of one's own perception." Master Cháng Bǎi: lying becomes a habit — as do killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct.

quiz.q: Among the ten, the treatise describes harsh speech through its opposite. Why, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: because this treatise belongs to the Mahāyāna bodhisattva canon
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Only harsh speech is introduced from the reverse side, chiefly because this treatise belongs to the Mahāyāna bodhisattva canon." §38 then briefly names venomous and coarse speech; the rest is "the reverse of the wholesome."

quiz.q: According to the treatise, into what three kinds are the twelve marks grouped?
options: speech of moral discipline (one), speech of equal delight (three), speech teaching the Dharma (the remaining eight)
quiz.why: "The first kind, speech subsumed under moral discipline, comprises the first alone … The second kind, speech that brings equal delight, comprises three … The third kind, speech that teaches the Dharma, comprises the remaining eight." The last splits into perfect destination (one), wording (two), and means (the rest). Venerable Miào Jìng: Dharma-speech runs from the fifth, "foremost," to the twelfth.
